claim_verdicts.source: Chrome headless (--dump-dom/--screenshot) run by reviewer on a scratch copy of stage-0 www/index.html + probe script
claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution only (no HTML/MDN docs root in content/versions.yaml, none under refs/). Chrome, index.html with 0 stylesheets: `H1 32px 700 rgb(0, 0, 0) | P 16px 400 | A rgb(0, 0, 238) underline`. Supports bigger/bold heading and coloured, underlined link for one browser. Lesson hardens this to "every browser" and "a link is still blue"; blue was observed only for an unvisited link, and the learner in section 2 has already clicked these links.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A page with no CSS of its own is not unstyled, though: the browser applies its own default styles, which is why a heading is still bigger and bold, and a link is still coloured and underlined.

claim_verdicts.evidence: No permitted source covers <head>/<title>/<body>: versions.yaml has no HTML or MDN docs root and refs/ holds only aspnetcore/docker/dotnet/efcore/flutter/kubernetes docs and rfc/. Headless Chrome cannot show a tab strip, so "the text on the browser tab" could not be observed by execution either. kind=fact, so not a blocker.

claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ stage-0: Caddyfile (:8080 block), docker-compose.yml (web, lab ports)
claim_verdicts.evidence: Caddyfile: `:8080 {` `root * /srv/www` ... final `handle { file_server }`. docker-compose.yml web service: `./www:/srv/www:ro`, `network_mode: "service:lab"`; lab publishes `"8080:8080"`. So http://localhost:8080/index.html is www/index.html served by Caddy.

No browser documentation is a permitted source (no key in versions.yaml, nothing in refs/). Ctrl+U / View page source cannot be exercised in headless Chrome. Wording is already hedged ("in most browsers"); kind=behavior, so not a blocker.

Framing sentence taken from outline items 1-3, hedged in the lesson ("usually built from three languages, each with one job"). Its stronger sibling in section 4 ("Without it, a loaded page stays exactly as it arrived") is not this claim and is raised as an issue.

issues.quote: Without it, a loaded page stays exactly as it arrived until you ask for another page.
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and false as written. Reviewer run: a page with no <script> and only `@keyframes k{from{opacity:1}to{opacity:0}} #g{animation:k 1s 1s forwards}` showed the <h1> at 100 ms and no <h1> at 4000 ms (Chrome headless screenshots) — CSS alone changed what was on screen after load. Hover styles and built-in HTML controls behave likewise. Outline item 4 is also absolute; the lesson must add the condition, not drop the idea.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Without it, HTML and CSS can only give the reactions the browser already has built in, such as a link loading a new page or a style that changes on hover. To decide for yourself what happens on a click, such as adding a welcome message, you need JavaScript." Add this as a claim (kind behavior) in .meta.json.

issues.quote: A link in plain HTML loads a new page; changing the current page in place needs JavaScript.
issues.text: Same overstatement as the section 4 major: CSS can change the current page in place (animation, hover) without JavaScript.
issues.fix: Rewrite line 5: "A link in plain HTML loads a new page; running your own code to change the current page, such as adding a message on a click, needs JavaScript."

issues.quote: Reacting to a click and changing the page without a new load is behaviour, which only JavaScript provides.
issues.text: Key (a) is correct given the lesson, but the explanation repeats the unconditioned "only JavaScript" that the section 4 major corrects; once the lesson is fixed the explanation will contradict it.
issues.fix: Change explanation.en.correct to: "Colour is how the heading looks, which is CSS's job. Running your own code on a click to add a message, without a new load, is behaviour, which is JavaScript's job." Mirror in vi.

issues.quote: the heading is large and bold and the links are blue and underlined
issues.text: "blue" is not in the ledger (claim 2 says "colored") and was observed only for an unvisited link (rgb(0, 0, 238)). Section 2 says the learner has already clicked these links many times; browsers render visited links in a different default colour, so the expected result can fail. Same word in section 4 ("a link is still blue").
issues.fix: Section 7: "the heading is large and bold and the links are coloured and underlined". Section 4: "a link is still coloured and underlined" (see claim 2 suggested_text).

issues.quote: Clicking a link loads another page from Caddy.
issues.text: Not true of all three links: Caddyfile at stage-0 answers `/redirect` with `redir * /index.html 302`, so that link ends on this same page.
issues.fix: "Clicking a link sends a new request to Caddy and loads whatever page comes back."

issues.quote: There is no `<style>` element and no `<link>` to a stylesheet, so no CSS of its own.
issues.text: "stylesheet" is not in known_vocab and not defined in Core concepts. I can guess it has to do with CSS, but not whether it is a separate file, what `<link>` does, or how it differs from `<style>`. It reappears in summary line 4 and in the q3 explanation, so I meet it three times without a definition.
issues.fix: In section 5, say it in plain words once: "no `<link>` pointing to a separate CSS file (a stylesheet)", and keep "stylesheet" only after that.

issues.quote: **HTML** — the markup language that structures a page's content
issues.text: "markup language" is a technical term I do not know. The rest of the sentence helps, but I stop on "markup" and wonder whether it means something beyond "structures content".
issues.fix: Replace "the markup language that structures" with "the language that marks up, i.e. labels, a page's content: this is a heading, this is a paragraph, this is a link", or simply "the language that structures".

issues.quote: A link or a form in plain HTML does make something happen, but what happens is a new request and a new page
issues.text: "form" is not in known_vocab and the lesson never shows or defines one. I do not know what an HTML form is or why it would send a request. It is not needed for the main idea, but it makes me stop.
issues.fix: Drop "or a form" here (and in the q2 correct explanation, "Its links and forms"), or add a half-sentence: "a form (input fields with a submit button)".

issues.text: The prose walks through `<head>`, `<title>`, `<body>` and the body elements, but says nothing about `<!doctype html>`, `<html lang="vi">` or `<meta charset="utf-8">`. I know encoding, so I can half-guess the meta line, but I am left wondering whether these three lines matter for the lesson.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before "`<head>` holds…": "The first lines say this is an HTML page in Vietnamese with UTF-8 encoding; you can ignore them for now."

issues.quote: Actually CSS changes how the content looks: size, color, position, whether it is shown at all.
issues.text: The correction itself raises my doubt: if CSS decides whether something is shown at all, then CSS does change what content I see, which is what the misconception says. The lesson does not say the hidden content is still in the HTML.
issues.fix: After "whether it is shown at all" add: "— and even hidden content is still there in the HTML, just not displayed."

issues.quote: You notice this when you remove a page's CSS and the same words and links are still there, only plainer.
issues.text: I have never removed a page's CSS and the lesson does not say how; the only page I have seen has no CSS to remove. The "you notice" moment is not one I can picture.
issues.fix: Tie it to what I have seen: "You notice this on `www/index.html`: it has no CSS of its own, yet every word and link is there."

issues.quote: "HTML alone can make a page interactive, the same way a button click can run code."
issues.text: "the same way a button click can run code" confuses me: which button, and run code where? The page has no button. I had to re-read to understand the misconception is "HTML can run code on a click".
issues.fix: Rephrase the belief as: "HTML alone can make something happen on the page when you click, without any code."

issues.text: Step 3 does not say how to search in the page-source view. Easy to guess, but steps 1-2 were explicit and this one is not.
issues.fix: Add "(Ctrl+F in the source view)" after "Search the source".

issues.quote: False, because a plain HTML link loads a new page instead of changing this one.
issues.text: The correct option is almost verbatim summary line 5 ("A link in plain HTML loads a new page") and is the longest option; option d ("HTML cannot contain links") is absurd after seeing the code. I can pick c from wording alone.
issues.fix: Reword c away from the summary wording (e.g. "False: clicking a link replaces the page rather than running code on it") and make d plausible, e.g. "False, because only buttons, not links, can react to clicks".

issues.quote: False, because the headings, text and links come from the HTML; CSS decides how they look.
issues.text: The correct option repeats the lesson's "The headings, text and links themselves come from the HTML" nearly word for word and is the longest; b ("CSS is where the page's text is written") and d ("CSS only works on pages that have JavaScript") are easy to dismiss. Guessable without understanding.
issues.fix: Paraphrase c (e.g. "False: take the CSS away and the same words and links remain") and make one wrong option plausible, e.g. "True, because CSS can hide an element".

skipped_steps: Section 6: "whether it is shown at all" — does not say hidden content still exists in the HTML, so the correction half-supports the misconception.
Section 5: `<!doctype html>`, `<html lang>` and `<meta charset>` lines are never mentioned in prose.
